title: Inside vs Outside Roulette Bets in Canada: Explained
excerpt: Inside or outside roulette bets? Canadian players can learn how each pays, how the house edge works and which style suits their bankroll and goals.
author: Lisa Davids
bodyHtml:
Roulette looks simple: a wheel spins, a ball lands, and you either win or lose. But the way you place your chips changes how often you win, how much you win and how quickly your bankroll moves. Understanding inside versus outside roulette bets is the foundation of playing the game sensibly in Canada, whether you prefer an online RNG table or a live dealer stream. This guide explains each bet type, what it pays, and how to match it to your style.

The layout: inside and outside bets

Every roulette table is divided into two areas. Inside bets are placed on the numbered grid itself and cover specific numbers or small groups of them. Outside bets are placed around the edge of the grid and cover large groups of numbers, such as all the reds, all the odds or a whole column.

The distinction matters because it controls volatility. Inside bets win rarely but pay a lot. Outside bets win often but pay modestly. Neither category changes the house edge on a given wheel, which is a point many players misunderstand. What you are really choosing is how bumpy the ride will be.

Inside bets explained

Inside bets give you the chance at big payouts from small stakes. The main types are straightforward once you see them laid out.

  • Straight up: a bet on a single number, paying 35 to 1.
  • Split: a bet on two adjacent numbers, paying 17 to 1.
  • Street: a bet on a row of three numbers, paying 11 to 1.
  • Corner: a bet on four numbers meeting at a point, paying 8 to 1.
  • Six line: a bet on two adjacent rows of three, paying 5 to 1.

Notice how the payouts shrink as the number of covered numbers grows. That is by design: the casino pays slightly less than the true odds of winning, and that gap is the house edge. A straight-up bet on a European wheel has 37 pockets but pays as though there were 36, which is where the built-in advantage comes from.

Who should use inside bets?

Inside bets suit players who enjoy the thrill of a long shot and can tolerate long losing runs. They work well with small stakes, since a single hit can cover many losing spins. They are not well suited to anyone trying to grind out a steady result, because the swings can be large.

Outside bets explained

Outside bets cover more of the wheel and win more often. The even-money options, red or black, odd or even, and high or low, pay 1 to 1 and cover just under half the numbers. Dozens and columns cover twelve numbers each and pay 2 to 1.

Because they hit so frequently, outside bets produce smaller, steadier fluctuations in your balance. That makes them a natural fit for players who want longer sessions on a modest budget. The trade-off is that your wins are small, and a single zero can interrupt a run, since the zero typically loses on most outside bets.

The role of the zero

The zero pocket is what gives the casino its edge. On an even-money bet, 18 numbers win, 18 lose and the zero (or zeros) also lose. On a European wheel with a single zero, the house edge is about 2.7 percent. On an American wheel with a zero and a double zero, it roughly doubles. Does any bet beat the house?

The honest answer is no. On a given wheel, nearly every standard bet carries the same house edge, so no placement is mathematically superior over the long run. Betting systems that promise to beat this, such as doubling after each loss, do not change the underlying odds. They simply shift risk, often turning many small wins into a rare but devastating loss when table limits or your bankroll run out.

Some special rules can improve things. Certain European tables use rules like En Prison or La Partage, which return half or all of an even-money stake when the ball lands on zero, reducing the effective edge on those bets. If a table offers them, they are worth seeking out. Always check the rules displayed at the table before you play.

Matching bets to your goals

The best approach depends on what you want from your session. If you want entertainment and a chance at a large win, a few small inside bets could fit. If you want to stretch a small bankroll over an evening, outside bets provide more steady action. Many experienced players blend the two, covering a dozen with an outside bet while placing a small amount on a couple of numbers.

Whatever mix you choose, decide on a budget and a session length before you start. Roulette moves quickly, especially online, and it is easy to place far more spins in an hour than you would at a land-based table. Setting a limit in advance keeps the game entertaining.

A simple example

Imagine you have a fixed session budget and a unit size you are comfortable with. Spreading it across outside bets means you might play for a long stretch with small ups and downs. Putting the same budget on single numbers could end in a handful of spins or a big win, and the expected loss per dollar wagered is the same. That is the heart of the inside versus outside choice: same cost, different shape of experience.

Playing roulette online in Canada

Online roulette comes in RNG versions, where software determines results, and live dealer versions streamed from a studio. Both use the same bet types, but live games add a social element and may include extra bonus features that change the payouts. Always read the paytable, since variants can alter the standard odds.

Key takeaways

Inside bets pay more but win less often, while outside bets win more often and pay less. The house edge stays the same across them on a given wheel, so choose based on how you want your session to feel rather than chasing a system. Check for favourable zero rules, avoid progression systems that disguise risk, and set a budget you can afford to lose before the first spin.
